newsitem.title: UK: ASDA says ready to match Tesco price cuts.
newsitem.headline: ASDA says ready to match Tesco price cuts.

text.p: British supermarket chain ASDA Plc will match price cuts by market leader Tesco Plc in order to maintain its price differential, chief executive Allan Leighton told Reuters in an interview.
"ASDA is very determined we will hold our position. It is very important for us to do that and we will hold it," he said.
Tesco announced earlier this month its "Unbeatable Value" campaign targeting 600 items over and above regular price offers and would match competitor prices on these.
ASDA aims to be around 10 percent cheaper for shoppers over a basket of goods and Leighton said the group would try to hold that differential.
"We have a reasonably wide gap between us and our competitors...we have no intention of letting that gap reduce," he said.
"If we are under pressure in some areas, we will and have and are responding," he added.
But he played down fears of a pre-Christmas price war.
"There is a bit of gearing up for Christmas, there is always a first salvo," he said.
